findings.failure_path: clear_shadow reopens the pathname after write_shadow has closed the descriptor it validated. If the populated shadow is renamed during the handler, cleanup can return on FileNotFoundError and leave the original inode full of transcript-derived content. If another owned, singly linked regular file occupies the name, cleanup can truncate that replacement as well.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep the validated shadow descriptor under the event’s ownership until cleanup. Truncate that descriptor before closing it. Add a lifecycle test that renames the populated shadow and verifies that the original inode is emptied and a replacement retains its contents.

findings.failure_path: Coverage receives the result content and skill lines but no requested ByteOffset. A misplaced result whose header and body agree with each other can therefore contribute coverage even when the paired call requested a different offset. The existing misplaced-start test changes the header relative to the body, so it misses this case.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass the paired call’s normalized ByteOffset into Partial validation and compare it with the reported start before applying UTF-8 back-off. Add a negative case that changes only the call offset and keeps the result intact.

findings.failure_path: Legacy temp cleanup uses an age check followed by an unlocked unlink. During mixed-version operation, an old writer can reopen a stale temp name after PID reuse and refresh it between those operations. The sweep then removes the active temp name, causing the old writer’s os.replace to fail.
findings.smallest_fix: Acquire the corresponding conversation run lock non-blockingly before removing a legacy temp. Recheck the entry’s identity, type and age under the lock. Extend the held-lock fixture to include a legacy temp.

findings.failure_path: os.scandir can open successfully and later raise OSError while advancing its iterator. The per-entry try starts after that advance. The exception can escape sweep_stale through write_shadow and send a new conversation’s first PreToolUse into fallback because directory cleanup failed.
findings.smallest_fix: Catch OSError around the entire scandir iteration. Add a test with an iterator that raises after yielding one entry and assert that the current event retains its normal verdict.

findings.failure_path: Every Partial result rebuilds and encodes every row in its claimed range, even when its size is invalid or its body is tiny. Accepted results also rescan the range and remerge accumulated spans. A transcript within the 32 MiB cap can thus cause repeated full-skill work while the event holds its run lock. The three-chunk tests do not establish a bound on that work.
findings.smallest_fix: Build the canonical bytes and row boundaries once per skill during replay, collect verified intervals, and merge them once per range. Add a fragmented-read regression that checks both coverage and a deterministic bound on full-range processing.

findings.failure_path: The release record marks the verifier and challenge finding fixed by a “challenge pass below,” but the file ends two lines later. It also gives no current-candidate outcomes for make test or the npm suite. A maintainer following this disposition could treat outstanding checks as complete.
findings.smallest_fix: Mark the disposition pending, record the actual verifier outcomes against the reviewed candidate, and link the challenge result with its outstanding findings before closing it.
